thread:
aeon: Hey team — first week here, trying to build the runtime from source on my dev workstation. Getting a bunch of ptxas arch warnings and then a link error. Anyone seen this before? Full run attached.

aeon: Command: `./build.sh --cuda /usr/local/cuda-12.1` 

aeon: Build output excerpt:
```
[ 72%] Linking CXX executable run_inference
/usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin/ptxas warning : Value 'sm_86' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so: undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
``` 

aeon: nvidia-smi shows CUDA Driver Version: 535.86.10, CUDA Version: 12.1

samir: welcome! :wave: first check: did you install the CUDA toolkit from packages or the runfile? some distros split libcuda vs toolkit.

samir: quick try: `ldd build/bin/run_inference | grep cuda` and `readelf -d build/bin/run_inference | grep RPATH`

mika: that ptxas warning is usually fine, but the undefined ref smells like mixed libcuda / driver mismatch or a missing --shared-libgcc link flag. which distro/ubuntu are you on?

aeon: ubuntu 22.04, installed via apt (cuda-toolkit-12-1). ldd shows libcublas.so -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so

eli: can you paste the exact linker command (add -v to ninja) — could be gcc vs g++ mismatch or --as-needed stripping symbols. also try setting `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before build.

devinfra-bot: Heads up — onboarding doc updated: https://redwood.internal/docs/onboard/runtime-dev-setup. Includes common CUDA versions and docker image tags.

samir: if apt install leaves you with a driver too new/old, the driver provides the libcuda.so — check `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*` and `modinfo nvidia | grep version`.

aeon: added LD_LIBRARY_PATH, re-ran, linker error changed to:
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/third_party/lib/libmycuda.a(cuda_kernels.o): undefined reference to `cuCtxGetCurrent'
``` 

aeon: I think maybe I linked static library (_a) causing missing runtime symbols.

mika: yep, that happens when you archive .o files that expect dynamic libcuda. Try linking against -lcuda -lcudart (dynamic) or build shared libmycuda.so

eli: if you're using our docker dev image, use `docker://redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12-1-gcc-12` — it sets up correct toolchain. if local, try `update-alternatives --config gcc` to ensure gcc/g++ pair match.

aeon: switched to the dev docker image and the build succeeded! :tada: still see ptxas warning but binary runs. Thanks all!

samir: awesome, welcome aboard. ping me if you want a quick pairing on local toolchain cleanup.

aeon: will do — thanks :heart:
